title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 166 (Bailee not responsible on re-delivery to bailor without title)

content.overview: Section 166 provides that if the bailor has no title to the goods, and the bailee, in good faith, delivers them back to, or according to the directions of, the bailor, the bailee is not responsible to the owner in respect of such delivery.
content.glance: Bailee who in good faith re-delivers goods to a bailor without title is not responsible to the true owner for that delivery.
content.study: If the bailor has no title to the goods, and the bailee, in good faith, delivers them back to, or according to the directions of, the bailor, the bailee is not responsible to the owner in respect of such delivery. Current-law framing: good-faith re-delivery to the person from whom the bailee received the goods protects the bailee.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If the bailor has no title to the goods, and the bailee, in good faith, delivers them back to, or according to the directions of, the bailor, the bailee is not responsible to the owner in respect of such delivery.

examples.title: Good-faith re-delivery
examples.body: Bailee returns goods in good faith to a bailor who lacked title. Bailee is not responsible to the true owner under Section 166.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee in good faith returns goods to a bailor who had no title. Is the bailee liable to the true owner?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 166 protects the bailee for such good-faith re-delivery.
